title: MET: Theory-Grounded and Culture-Aware Multilingual Moral Reasoning
inspected: PDF pp.3–7, §§3–4.2; official code revision130007d875fbb8a19bdebe8091c8925a694849c9 inherited inspection; paper body rechecked this review
data: MCLASH culturally adapts long scenarios into six languages including Spanish; character priorities provide decision labels.
method: Select situation-specific grounds, then reason. MET-D rejection-samples self-distillation data. Normative authority, value system, ethical theory and reasoning strategy are separate dimensions.
limit: Decision task, not expert conditional-similarity or harm–response retrieval; language serves as a cultural proxy.
jep: Keep harm value fixed while varying declared theory; Spanish coverage does not establish Colombian victim/cultural validity.
gap_confidence: moderate: conditional JEP retrieval not evaluated in inspected methods

title: Structured Moral Reasoning in Language Models: A Value-Grounded Evaluation Framework
authors: Mohna Chakraborty, Lu Wang, David Jurgens
data: Twelve open models and four curated English moral datasets.
method: Combines value systems, ethical theories and cognitive strategies; reasoning-based supervised distillation.
limit: Static single-turn evaluation; teacher coherence bounds distillation; underrepresented normative traditions not exhausted.
jep: Theory scaffolding and reasoning distillation are established ingredients; compare them with factual evidence extraction rather than asserting novelty.
gap_confidence: high on ingredient already covered; moderate on domain-specific transfer gap

title: Morality is Non-Binary: Building a Pluralist Moral Sentence Embedding Space using Contrastive Learning
authors: Jeongwoo Park, Enrico Liscio, Pradeep K. Murukannaiah
data: Moral Foundations Twitter Corpus; human multi-label moral-element annotations.
method: Supervised/unsupervised SimCSE; positives share moral labels; opposite/outside policies choose negatives.
limit: Fixed MFT taxonomy and topical social-media domains; opposite labels do not specify appropriate reparative responses.
jep: A moral embedding space is not new. Harm–repair relations require separate labels from care-versus-harm sentiment.
gap_confidence: high on moral embedding precedent; moderate on relational extension

title: Can we Use Conceptual Spaces to Model Moral Principles?
data: Ten technology-ethics vignettes;392 retained engineering students across two surveys.
method: Pairwise moral similarity plus principle applicability; MDS and individual-difference dimension weights.
limit: Aggregate common space can mask different notions of moral similarity and respondent weighting.
jep: Explicitly condition expert comparisons and preserve disagreement instead of calling one pooled geometry moral truth.
gap_confidence: high on direct precedent; moderate on proposed conditional-human extension

title: Measuring structural value alignment in sixteen models: LLMs have human-like moral spaces
data: Same ten moral cases and human baseline; model outputs under exemplar/no-exemplar conditions.
method: MDS, principle regions, space-overlap and Procrustes case displacement.
limit: Sparse cases, human baseline dependence, dimensionality and exemplar anchoring; outputs do not establish internal representations.
jep: Global moral-space reconstruction already exists; require family transfer and task utility rather than another attractive map.
gap_confidence: high on precedent; moderate on held-out conditional retrieval gap

title: Do Morals Guide How LLMs Think? The Role of Ethical Perspectives in General Problem Solving
authors: Iseo Kim, Eunjin Hong, Juae Kim
data: Kohlberg-derived conditions checked with DIT; general reasoning via MMLU.
method: Final-token hidden states at every Llama3-8B layer; moral-conditioned versus baseline cosine; structurally matched non-moral role controls.
limit: Representation shifts under broad moral-development frames are not evidence of condition-specific harm retrieval.
jep: Layerwise moral-conditioning plots are not novel; matched role/length controls are essential.
gap_confidence: high: direct counterexample to generic layer novelty

title: Probing Ethical Framework Representations in Large Language Models: Structure, Entanglement, and Methodological Challenges
authors: Weilun Xu, Alexander Rusnak, Frédéric Kaplan
data: ETHICS partitions across six language models.
method: Layer-specific linear probes and cross-framework transfer; conflict compared with behavioral variability.
limit: Paraphrase failures reveal template signatures; steering changed position preference without improving ethical accuracy; difficulty confound remains.
jep: Use identical facts across theories and held-out paraphrases/domains. Decodability alone cannot support a moral mechanism.
gap_confidence: high on confounds; moderate on within-case factorial extension

title: Learning Human-like Representations to Enable Learning Human Values
authors: Andrea H. Wynn, Ilia Sucholutsky, Thomas L. Griffiths
data: Fifty ETHICS-derived action descriptions; human morality/similarity judgments; embedding and LLM similarity models.
method: Representational alignment as similarity correlation; kernel-based learning and bandit generalization.
limit: Moral value approximated by scalar actions; alignment utility is not specific to restorative narratives.
jep: Similarity geometry improving value learning already has precedent. Measure concrete expert retrieval gains and separate similarity from decision value.

title: Agreement Is Not Alignment: Divergent Moral Grounds in Human and LLM Ethical Judgments
data: Curated500 ETHICS-derived English items; three annotations per item from five broadly Central-European annotators.
method: Final judgments plus structured rationale categories; agreement and rationale-profile deviation.
limit: Expressed rationales are not causal internal reasoning; limited culture/sample; two partitions lack comparable structured rationale coding.
jep: Judge evidence/grounds and retrieval separately from verdict labels; preserve minority rationales.
gap_confidence: high on label/rationale distinction; bibliographic date metadata unresolved

title: On the Context Sensitivity of LLM Moral Judgment
data: Contextual MoralChoice:302 base scenarios and consequentialist/emotional/relational variants;22 models.
method: Marginalized prompt/answer orders; human contextual comparison; contrastive final-token activation differences steer sensitivity.
limit: Rule-violation decisions rather than similarity retrieval; relevant sensitivity can differ between humans and models.
jep: Context-difference vectors and steering already exist. Test theory-selective sensitivity and harm evidence, not mere movement.
